brief:
Netanyahu's Likud party and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc resumed coalition negotiations Sunday as Israel seeks to form a government, Al-Monitor reported. The talks represent a fresh attempt to bridge differences between the caretaker prime minister's camp and his political rival after previous negotiations stalled.

Netanyahu's party has prioritized maintaining his core policies as a condition for any power-sharing arrangement. The outcome of these discussions will determine whether the two blocs can reach an agreement to establish a governing coalition.
dek: The parties of caretaker Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks on Sunday over whether to form a coalition government, with Netanyahu's party insisting on keeping his main policies.
title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot parties resume coalition talks
